html:
The Danggali were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry country on the border between South Australia and New South Wales, south of Broken Hill. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is mallee, bluebush and saltbush plain with few permanent waters. Little is recorded of them, but Danggali Conservation Park in South Australia keeps their name. Neighbours on the map include the Wilyakali, the Barkindji and the Ngadjuri. Sheep stations spread into this country in the second half of the 1800s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
